_provenance: National (UK-wide) figures for Tax Year 2025/26 (6 April 2025 – 5 April 2026), per HMRC published rates. UK income tax: personal allowance £12,570 (0%), basic 20% to £50,270, higher 40% to £125,140, additional 45% above. Capital gains: the UK has NO long-term/short-term holding-period split — CGT applies on disposal of most assets regardless of holding period, at 18% (basic) or 24% (higher) on other assets (rates effective from 30 October 2024), with an annual exempt amount of £3,000 for 2025/26. The engine models a single marginal CGT rate (see notes), so this pack uses the FLAT_NO_HOLDING_PERIOD shape with the 18% basic rate; the £3,000 AEA and 24% higher rate are recorded here but not modelled at national level (consistent with docs/05-jurisdiction-tax-framework.md §5.7).

incomeTax.note: UK 2025/26 income tax (as taxable income after the personal allowance): 0% to £12,570 (personal allowance); 20% to £50,270; 40% to £125,140; 45% above. The top bracket's 'upTo' uses a large finite sentinel since the schema requires a number. The engine prices retirement-year drawdown via marginalRateAtRetirement (a single planning assumption), set here to the basic 20% rate typical of retirement.

capitalGains.note: UK CGT has no long/short-term holding-period split, so these use the FLAT_NO_HOLDING_PERIOD shape at the 18% basic rate (24% applies to higher-rate taxpayers). The £3,000 annual exempt amount and the higher rate are not modelled at national level. UK allows capital-loss offsetting (lossOffsetAllowed true).

yieldIncome.note: UK dividends have their own rates (8.75% basic, 33.75% higher, 39.35% additional) above a £500 dividend allowance for 2025/26; interest above the savings allowance is taxed as ordinary income. The engine keeps yield income structurally separate; simplified treatments below.

withdrawalWaterfall.note: Tax-free / tax-advantaged accounts (Cash, NS&I bonds) are drawn first, then taxable investment accounts, with the pension (SIPP) drawn last since withdrawals are taxed as income.
